r-0001.title: Tenant Protection Act rent cap (Civ. Code 1947.12, SB 567 version)
r-0001.requirement: Rent cannot be raised more than 5% plus the regional CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period, measured from the lowest rent in the prior 12 months, and in no more than two increments. A new tenancy may start at any rent.
r-0001.coverage_conditions: Residential real property not exempt; increases on or after 2019-03-15; section repealed 2030-01-01
r-0001.exemptions: Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; school dormitories; housing under local rent control that limits increases below this cap; certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years; separately alienable unit (single-family home or condo) of a non-REIT, non-corporate owner who gave the statutory notice; owner-occupied duplex; mobilehome homeowners
r-0001.interaction: Yields to local rent control that restricts increases below the state cap (subd. (d)(3)): LA RSO, San Francisco, Berkeley, Santa Ana; San Diego has no local cap. Section operative 2024-04-01 per subd. (n) (SB 567, effective 2024-01-01). D040 (LAHD JCO page) restates the same cap and was merged here.
r-0001.quoted_span: shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower

all.unavailable: unit alienable separately (single-family home or condo) owned by a non-REIT, non-corporate owner who gave the statutory exemption notice
owner occupied one of the two units as principal residence since the start of the tenancy, neither unit an ADU

r-0001.title_es: Límite de aumentos de alquiler de la Tenant Protection Act (Civ. Code 1947.12, versión SB 567)
r-0001.requirement_es: El alquiler no puede aumentarse más del 5% más el cambio del IPC regional, o el 10%, el que sea menor, en cualquier período de 12 meses, medido desde el alquiler más bajo de los 12 meses anteriores, y en no más de dos incrementos. Un nuevo arrendamiento puede comenzar con cualquier alquiler.

r-0002.title: Tenant Protection Act just cause for eviction (Civ. Code 1946.2, AB 1529 version)
r-0002.requirement: After a tenant has lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months (24 months if an adult tenant was added), the owner may end the tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. For a no-fault cause the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent.
r-0002.key_value: just cause after 12 months; 1 month's rent relocation for no-fault
r-0002.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies after 12 months of continuous lawful occupancy (24 months if adult tenants were added); section repealed 2030-01-01
r-0002.exemptions: Transient hotels; nonprofit hospital, religious, care facilities; school dormitories; tenant sharing bath or kitchen with resident owner; owner-occupied single-family home renting up to two units or bedrooms; owner-occupied duplex; certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years; separately alienable unit of a non-REIT, non-corporate owner with notice; deed-restricted affordable housing; property covered by a qualifying local just cause ordinance
r-0002.interaction: Does not apply where a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before 2019-09-01, or a later more protective one, covers the property (subd. (i)); yields to the LA, San Diego, Santa Ana, San Francisco and Berkeley just cause rules. Section operative 2024-04-01 per subd. (m); current text amended by AB 1529, effective 2026-01-01.
r-0002.quoted_span: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause

all.unavailable: single-family owner-occupied residence renting no more than two units or bedrooms
owner occupied one of the two units as principal residence since the start of the tenancy, neither unit an ADU
unit alienable separately (single-family home or condo) owned by a non-REIT, non-corporate owner who gave the statutory exemption notice

r-0002.title_es: Desalojo con causa justificada de la Tenant Protection Act (Civ. Code 1946.2, versión AB 1529)
r-0002.requirement_es: Después de que un inquilino haya ocupado legalmente una unidad durante 12 meses (24 meses si se agregó un inquilino adulto), el propietario solo puede poner fin al arrendamiento por una causa justificada, con culpa o sin culpa, indicada en el aviso. Para una causa sin culpa, el propietario debe pagar un mes de alquiler como asistencia de reubicación o renunciar al alquiler del último mes.
r-0002.key_value_es: causa justificada después de 12 meses; reubicación de 1 mes de alquiler para causas sin culpa

r-0003.title: Security deposit cap of one month's rent (Civ. Code 1950.5 as amended by AB 12)
r-0003.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent; a qualifying small landlord may take up to two months. The deposit must be returned with an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out.
r-0003.key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords)
r-0003.coverage_conditions: Security for residential rental agreements collected or demanded on or after 2024-07-01
r-0003.exemptions: Not an exemption but a variant: a landlord who is a natural person (or LLC of natural persons) owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units in total may take up to two months' rent, except from a service member; advance payment of six months' rent or more allowed for leases of six months or longer
r-0003.interaction: Statewide; no local deposit cap found for the CA1 cities. The cap applies to security collected on or after 2024-07-01 per subd. (c)(6); the section was last amended by AB 414 (effective 2026-01-01, photo and return rules). LA RSO units also earn deposit interest under L.A.M.C. 151.06.02.
r-0003.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent
r-0003.title_es: Límite del depósito de seguridad a un mes de alquiler (Civ. Code 1950.5 modificado por AB 12)
r-0003.requirement_es: Un arrendador no puede exigir ni recibir una garantía de más de un mes de alquiler, además del alquiler del primer mes; un pequeño arrendador que califique puede cobrar hasta dos meses. El depósito debe devolverse con un estado de cuenta detallado dentro de los 21 días posteriores a la mudanza.
r-0003.key_value_es: 1 mes de alquiler (2 meses para pequeños arrendadores que califiquen)

r-0004.title: Application screening fee cap (Civ. Code 1950.6)
r-0004.requirement: A landlord may charge an application screening fee only for actual out-of-pocket screening costs, never more than $30 per applicant adjusted for CPI since 1998, and only when a unit is or will soon be available. The landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, and either process applications first-come or refund applicants not selected.
r-0004.coverage_conditions: Landlords and agents charging applicants (including guarantors and cosigners) to screen residential rental applications
r-0004.interaction: Statewide; the fee is not security under 1950.5. The text gives no current CPI-adjusted dollar figure and no single official 2026 figure exists (starter README section 9). effective_date is the AB 1170 amendment (2026-01-01); the $30 cap itself is older.
r-0004.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
r-0004.title_es: Límite de la tarifa de evaluación de solicitud (Civ. Code 1950.6)
r-0004.requirement_es: Un arrendador puede cobrar una tarifa de evaluación de solicitud solo por los costos reales de evaluación, nunca más de $30 por solicitante ajustados por el IPC desde 1998, y solo cuando una unidad está disponible o lo estará pronto. El arrendador debe entregar un recibo detallado, reembolsar los montos no usados y procesar las solicitudes por orden de llegada o reembolsar a los solicitantes no seleccionados.
r-0004.key_value_es: $30 por solicitante, ajustado por el IPC

r-0005.title: FEHA housing discrimination: source of income, including vouchers (Gov. Code 12955, SB 329 / SB 267)
r-0005.requirement: Owners may not discriminate against or harass anyone because of source of income, including Section 8 and other housing vouchers (since SB 329, 2020-01-01), and since SB 267 (2024-01-01) must offer an alternative to credit history when there is a rent subsidy. CRD guidance adds that blanket criminal-history bans are unlawful and arrests without conviction, sealed or juvenile records may not be considered.
r-0005.key_value: source-of-income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) discrimination barred; no blanket criminal-history bans
r-0005.coverage_conditions: Owners of housing accommodations and others in real estate transactions in California
r-0005.exemptions: Owner-occupant renting to one additional person may choose among applicants (but may not publish discriminatory statements); senior housing may limit by age
r-0005.interaction: Statewide floor; LA (L.A.M.C. 45.65 to 45.69) and San Diego (S.D.M.C. 98.0801 to 98.0806) add local source-of-income rules. effective_date 2020-01-01 is when SB 329 made vouchers part of source of income (X021, secondary; the brief names this cell 'FEHA (SB 329)'); the current text, incl. the credit-history alternative, is the SB 267 amendment effective 2024-01-01 (D027). Criminal-history limits come from CRD guidance (D016) that cites no section, so they are folded in here.
r-0005.quoted_span: For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income

all.unavailable: owner occupies the home and rents to only one additional person

r-0005.title_es: Discriminación en la vivienda según la FEHA: fuente de ingresos, incluidos los vales (Gov. Code 12955, SB 329 / SB 267)
r-0005.requirement_es: Los propietarios no pueden discriminar ni acosar a nadie por su fuente de ingresos, incluidos Section 8 y otros vales de vivienda, y con un subsidio de alquiler deben ofrecer una alternativa al historial de crédito. La guía del CRD añade que las prohibiciones generales por antecedentes penales son ilegales y que no pueden considerarse arrestos sin condena, registros sellados ni de menores.
r-0005.key_value_es: se prohíbe la discriminación por fuente de ingresos (incl. vales de Section 8); sin prohibiciones generales por antecedentes penales

r-0006.title: Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms (AB 325 and SB 763)
r-0006.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend or set a price) as part of a price-fixing agreement, or while coercing others to adopt its recommended prices or terms. Not limited to housing; covers shared rent-setting software. SB 763 raised penalties, including civil fines up to $1 million in AG or district attorney actions.
r-0006.key_value: ban on common pricing algorithms using competitor data; civil fines up to $1 million
r-0006.coverage_conditions: Any person using or distributing a common pricing algorithm in California; not rental-specific
r-0006.exemptions: End consumers are not covered persons
r-0006.interaction: Effective date evidence: D022 shows AB 325 chaptered 2025-10-06 (Ch. 338) and its text gives no effective date; 2026-01-01 comes from organizer test T1 (data/dev/change_tests.json), the Cleary Gottlieb alert X024 and the brief (1/1/2026). Statewide antitrust rule that sits alongside the local bans in San Francisco, San Diego, Berkeley and Santa Ana.
r-0006.quoted_span: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
r-0006.title_es: Prohibición de algoritmos comunes de fijación de precios de la Cartwright Act (AB 325 y SB 763)
r-0006.requirement_es: Es ilegal usar o distribuir un algoritmo de precios común (software o método usado por dos o más personas que utiliza datos de competidores para recomendar o fijar un precio) como parte de un acuerdo de fijación de precios, o mientras se coacciona a otros para que adopten sus precios o condiciones recomendados. No se limita a la vivienda; abarca el software compartido de fijación de alquileres. SB 763 aumentó las sanciones, incluidas multas civiles de hasta $1 millón en acciones de la AG o de un fiscal de distrito.
r-0006.key_value_es: prohibición de algoritmos de precios comunes que usan datos de competidores; multas civiles de hasta $1 millón

all.unavailable: owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units

r-0007.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act
r-0007.requirement: A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or refuse to renew a lease without one of the good causes listed in the Act, and must prove that cause in court. Most causes require a written Notice to Quit, and some a Notice to Cease first.
r-0007.key_value: Good cause required for eviction or non-renewal (statutory grounds); Notice to Quit for all causes except nonpayment
r-0007.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental properties, including single-family homes, apartment buildings and complexes, mobile homes, rooming and boarding homes
r-0007.exemptions: Two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units; transient or seasonal hotel, motel or guest house guests; unit held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies it
r-0007.quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a
r-0007.interaction: Statewide; applies alongside local rent control in Jersey City, Hoboken and Newark. Quote from the supplied DCA guide (D067); statute text X011 (supplemental) confirms the grounds and the owner-occupied two-rental-unit exception but gives no effective date for the current version.
r-0007.title_es: NJ Anti-Eviction Act (Ley contra el Desalojo de Nueva Jersey)
r-0007.requirement_es: Un arrendador residencial no puede desalojar a un inquilino ni negarse a renovar un contrato de arrendamiento sin una de las causas justificadas enumeradas en la Ley, y debe probar esa causa ante el tribunal. La mayoría de las causas requieren un Notice to Quit (aviso de desocupación) por escrito, y algunas un Notice to Cease (aviso de cese) previo.
r-0007.key_value_es: Se requiere causa justificada para el desalojo o la no renovación (causas legales); Notice to Quit para todas las causas excepto la falta de pago

all.unavailable: owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units and the tenant has not invoked the law by 30 days written notice

r-0008.title: NJ Security Deposit Law
r-0008.requirement: A landlord may not take a security deposit above 1.5 times one month's rent, and a yearly top-up may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. The deposit must be held in a New Jersey interest-bearing account, interest belongs to the tenant, and it must be returned with interest less itemized deductions within 30 days after the tenancy ends.
r-0008.coverage_conditions: All rental premises or units used for dwelling purposes (N.J.S.A. 46:8-26)
r-0008.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling (owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units), unless the tenant gives 30 days written notice invoking the law; interest-account rules do not apply to seasonal rentals of 125 days or less
r-0008.quoted_span: one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less.
r-0008.interaction: Statewide. Quote from the supplied DCA guide (D067); statute texts X012 (46:8-21.2, cap and 10% rule, history 'amended 2003, c.188', a year not an effective date) and X013 (46:8-26, coverage section of the same act) merged into this one record.
r-0008.title_es: NJ Security Deposit Law (Ley de Depósitos de Seguridad de Nueva Jersey)
r-0008.requirement_es: Un arrendador no puede cobrar un depósito de seguridad superior a 1.5 veces un mes de alquiler, y un aumento anual no puede exceder el 10% del depósito actual. El depósito debe mantenerse en una cuenta con intereses en Nueva Jersey, los intereses pertenecen al inquilino, y debe devolverse con intereses, menos las deducciones detalladas, dentro de los 30 días posteriores al fin del arrendamiento.
r-0008.key_value_es: 1.5 meses de alquiler; aumento anual máximo del 10% del depósito actual

r-0009.title: Residential rental application fee cap
r-0009.requirement: A landlord or agent may not charge an application or similar fee above $50 to apply to rent a home; the cap is adjusted each January 1 by CPI. Violations carry penalties and the overcharge is returned to the applicant.
r-0009.coverage_conditions: Application or similar fee to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes
r-0009.exemptions: Dwelling unit in a one-family or two-family dwelling; a New Jersey Real Estate Commission licensee unless the licensee is the landlord
r-0009.quoted_span: shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50.
r-0009.interaction: Statewide (C.46:8-18.1). Effective date computed from section 3 (first day of the fourth month after approval on January 20, 2026), matching the brief (eff. 5/1/2026). The licensee carve-out concerns who charges the fee, not the building, so it is not in exempt_if.
r-0009.title_es: Límite de la tarifa de solicitud de alquiler residencial
r-0009.requirement_es: Un arrendador o agente no puede cobrar una tarifa de solicitud o similar superior a $50 por solicitar el alquiler de una vivienda; el límite se ajusta cada 1 de enero según el IPC. Las infracciones conllevan sanciones y el cobro en exceso se devuelve al solicitante.
r-0009.key_value_es: límite de $50, ajustado anualmente por el IPC; sanción de hasta $500 / $750 / $1,000

all.unavailable: owner occupies the other unit of a two-family dwelling, or rents rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling

r-0010.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination: source of lawful income
r-0010.requirement: A landlord may not refuse to rent or treat an applicant differently because of the source of lawful income or rent payment, such as a Section 8 voucher. A landlord may still refuse for insufficient income or poor credit.
r-0010.key_value: Source of lawful income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) is a protected basis
r-0010.coverage_conditions: Sale or rental of all real property, residential or business
r-0010.exemptions: Single apartment in a two-family dwelling whose other unit the owner occupies; rooms rented in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling; religious-organization preference; housing for older persons (familial status only)
r-0010.quoted_span: a landlord cannot deny the lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful income.
r-0010.interaction: Separate instrument from the Fair Chance in Housing Act in the same cell. Quote from the DCR brochure (D068); the cite N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h) is printed in the DCA guide (D067), which also lists source of lawful income as protected. Neither text gives an effective date.
r-0010.title_es: NJ Law Against Discrimination: fuente de ingresos lícitos (Ley contra la Discriminación de Nueva Jersey)
r-0010.requirement_es: Un arrendador no puede negarse a alquilar ni dar un trato diferente a un solicitante por su fuente de ingresos lícitos o de pago del alquiler, como un vale de Section 8. El arrendador aún puede negarse por ingresos insuficientes o mal crédito.
r-0010.key_value_es: La fuente de ingresos lícitos (incl. vales de Section 8) es una base protegida

r-0011.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act
r-0011.requirement: Landlords may not ask about criminal history on an application or before making a conditional offer. After the offer they may consider only certain convictions within set lookback periods, must do an individualized assessment, and must give written reasons if they withdraw the offer.
r-0011.key_value: No criminal-record inquiry before a conditional offer; lookback 6 years (1st degree), 4 years (2nd/3rd degree), 1 year (4th degree); penalties up to $1,000 / $5,000 / $10,000
r-0011.coverage_conditions: Housing providers offering a rental dwelling unit for residential purposes
r-0011.exemptions: Dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units
r-0011.quoted_span: shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
r-0011.interaction: Statewide (C.46:8-52 et seq.); the text contains no preemption clause, so it applies alongside Newark's ban-the-box ordinance. Effective date computed from section 14 (first day of the seventh month after approval on June 18, 2021).
r-0011.title_es: Fair Chance in Housing Act (Ley de Segunda Oportunidad en la Vivienda)
r-0011.requirement_es: Los arrendadores no pueden preguntar por antecedentes penales en una solicitud ni antes de hacer una oferta condicional. Después de la oferta, solo pueden considerar ciertas condenas dentro de períodos de revisión establecidos, deben hacer una evaluación individualizada y deben dar razones por escrito si retiran la oferta.
r-0011.key_value_es: Sin preguntas sobre antecedentes penales antes de una oferta condicional; período de revisión de 6 años (1.er grado), 4 años (2.o y 3.er grado), 1 año (4.o grado); sanciones de hasta $1,000 / $5,000 / $10,000

r-0012.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
r-0012.requirement: From July 1, 2027, landlords may not pay for or use a coordinator's rent-setting service that pools competitors' nonpublic data or sets rents, lease terms or occupancy by algorithm, and no one may perform that coordinating function. Violations are violations of the New Jersey Antitrust Act.
r-0012.key_value: Ban on algorithmic coordination of rents, lease terms or occupancy using competitors' nonpublic data; effective 2027-07-01
r-0012.coverage_conditions: Rental property owners, coordinators and their agents; any residential dwelling unit used as a primary residence in New Jersey
r-0012.exemptions: Inpatient medical, long-term care and detention facilities are not dwelling units; research or testing use; free public rent estimates; equal-terms brokerage listing databases; government affordability controls; non-AI spreadsheets needing human analysis and plain database queries
r-0012.quoted_span: a rental property owner, or any agent, representative, or subcontractor thereof, to receive, subscribe to, contract for, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of, the services of a coordinator;
r-0012.interaction: Possible preemption of the Jersey City and Hoboken bans, for human review: section 6.b reads "A municipality shall be prohibited from enacting an ordinance that conflicts with this act." and adds that it does not bar ordinances explicitly authorized or required by other law; it does not say whether ordinances enacted before the act are void. Approved July 20, 2026; effective date computed from section 9 (first day of the twelfth month after enactment), matching the brief, T3 and X025.
r-0012.title_es: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act (Ley que Prohíbe la Inflación Algorítmica del Alquiler)
r-0012.requirement_es: A partir del 1 de julio de 2027, los arrendadores no pueden pagar ni usar el servicio de fijación de alquileres de un coordinador que reúna datos no públicos de competidores o fije alquileres, condiciones del contrato u ocupación mediante un algoritmo, y nadie puede realizar esa función de coordinación. Las infracciones constituyen infracciones de la New Jersey Antitrust Act.
r-0012.key_value_es: Prohibición de la coordinación algorítmica de alquileres, condiciones del contrato u ocupación con datos no públicos de competidores; vigente desde 2027-07-01

r-0013.exemptions: Narrow exception for a town that accepts c.40P: voluntary-only regulation, not for owners of fewer than ten units or units with fair market rent above $400, owners compensated by the town
r-0013.interaction: Bars local rent control in Boston and Cambridge; statute text carries no effective date. The 2026 ballot question to repeal it (IP 25-21) was struck, see MA-02.
r-0013.title: State bar on local rent control (M.G.L. c.40P s.4)
r-0013.requirement: Massachusetts cities and towns may not enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, so there is no local rent cap in Boston or Cambridge. Massachusetts also has no statewide rent cap.
r-0013.key_value: Local rent control prohibited; no statewide cap
r-0013.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind
r-0013.title_es: Prohibición estatal del control local de alquileres (M.G.L. c.40P s.4)
r-0013.requirement_es: Las ciudades y pueblos de Massachusetts no pueden promulgar, mantener ni hacer cumplir control de alquileres de ningún tipo, por lo que no hay un límite local de alquiler en Boston ni en Cambridge. Massachusetts tampoco tiene un límite de alquiler a nivel estatal.
r-0013.key_value_es: Control local de alquileres prohibido; sin límite estatal

r-0014.coverage_conditions: Would have covered most residential rental units statewide
r-0014.exemptions: Proposed: owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, units under 10 years old, certain regulated units, short-term rentals, educational, religious or nonprofit facilities
r-0014.interaction: Supplemental source (no supplied D doc covers it; D059 was link-only): X023 for the petition number and terms, X007 (WBUR, 2026-06-23) and organizer test T5 for the struck status. Evidence that no rent cap applies in Boston or Cambridge; M.G.L. c.40P s.4 stays in force.
r-0014.title: Initiative Petition 25-21, An Initiative Petition to Protect Tenants by Limiting Rent Increases (struck from 2026 ballot)
r-0014.requirement: A 2026 ballot question would have repealed the c.40P ban and capped annual rent increases. The Supreme Judicial Court removed it from the November 2026 ballot on 2026-06-23 (Cella v. Attorney General), so it is not law and no rent cap applies.
r-0014.key_value: Failed: proposed cap of the lesser of CPI or 5% never took effect
r-0014.quoted_span: The case, Cella v. Attorney General, SJC-13893 (embedded below), involved Initiative Petition 25-21
r-0014.title_es: Initiative Petition 25-21, An Initiative Petition to Protect Tenants by Limiting Rent Increases (eliminada de la boleta de 2026)
r-0014.requirement_es: Una pregunta de la boleta de 2026 habría derogado la prohibición de c.40P y limitado los aumentos anuales de alquiler. La Supreme Judicial Court la retiró de la boleta de noviembre de 2026 el 2026-06-23 (Cella v. Attorney General), por lo que no es ley y no se aplica ningún límite de alquiler.
r-0014.key_value_es: Fallida: el límite propuesto del menor entre el IPC o el 5% nunca entró en vigor

r-0015.exemptions: Leases or tenancies of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes
r-0015.interaction: Statewide; no Boston or Cambridge deposit rule found. Effective date is the 2025 c.9 amendment of clause (1)(b) (adds lessor's agents, fee in lieu of deposit capped with the deposit at 1 month's rent); the one-month cap itself is older.
r-0015.title: Security deposits (M.G.L. c.186 s.15B)
r-0015.requirement: A security deposit may not exceed the first month's rent. The landlord must give receipts and a statement of condition, hold the deposit in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, pay interest yearly and return it within 30 days with an itemized sworn list of any deductions; violations can cost three times the deposit.
r-0015.quoted_span: (iii) a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3)
r-0015.requirement_es: Un depósito de seguridad no puede exceder el alquiler del primer mes. El arrendador debe dar recibos y una declaración del estado de la vivienda, mantener el depósito en una cuenta bancaria separada con intereses en Massachusetts, pagar intereses cada año y devolverlo dentro de los 30 días con una lista detallada y jurada de cualquier deducción; las infracciones pueden costar el triple del depósito.

r-0016.coverage_conditions: Licensed brokers or salespersons finding rental housing for a fee
r-0016.interaction: Statute text marks this version as amended by 2025 c.9 s.43, effective August 1, 2025. Separate instrument from the c.186 s.15B upfront-charge limit (MA-04).
r-0016.title: Broker fee paid by the party who hired the broker (M.G.L. c.112 s.87DDD1/2)
r-0016.requirement: A rental broker works for either the tenant or the landlord, and any broker fee is paid only by the party who hired the broker, so a tenant does not pay a broker the landlord engaged.
r-0016.key_value: Broker fee paid only by the party that engaged the broker
r-0016.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.
r-0016.title_es: Límite de cobros iniciales (M.G.L. c.186 s.15B(1)(b))
r-0016.requirement_es: En la mudanza o antes, un arrendador o su agente solo puede cobrar el alquiler del primer mes, el alquiler del último mes, un depósito de seguridad de hasta un mes de alquiler y el costo de una cerradura y llave nuevas. No se permiten tarifas de solicitud ni de evaluación cobradas por el arrendador.
r-0016.key_value_es: Solo primer mes, último mes, depósito, cerradura y llave; sin tarifa de solicitud

r-0017.coverage_conditions: Lessors and agents of the lessor, at or before the start of a residential tenancy
r-0017.exemptions: Leases or tenancies of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes
r-0017.interaction: Same statute as the deposit rule (MA-03), recorded here for the upfront-charge limit; X022 (secondary) confirms landlords may not charge application fees. Current text of clause (1)(b) effective 2025-08-01 (2025 c.9). Broker fees are governed separately by M.G.L. c.112 s.87DDD1/2 (MA-05).
r-0017.title: Limit on upfront charges (M.G.L. c.186 s.15B(1)(b))
r-0017.requirement: At or before move-in, a landlord or the landlord's agent may charge only first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of up to one month's rent and the cost of a new lock and key. Application and screening fees charged by the landlord are not allowed.
r-0017.key_value: Only first month, last month, deposit, lock and key; no application fee
r-0017.quoted_span: (b) At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:
r-0017.title_es: Honorarios del corredor pagados por la parte que lo contrató (M.G.L. c.112 s.87DDD1/2)
r-0017.requirement_es: Un corredor de alquileres trabaja para el inquilino o para el arrendador, y cualquier honorario del corredor lo paga solo la parte que lo contrató, por lo que un inquilino no paga a un corredor contratado por el arrendador.
r-0017.key_value_es: Honorarios del corredor pagados solo por la parte que contrató al corredor

r-0018.interaction: Statewide floor; Boston and Cambridge add local source-of-income protections. No effective date in the text. Criminal-record screening is recorded separately under 803 CMR 5.00 (MA-12).
r-0018.title: Source of income and housing subsidy discrimination (M.G.L. c.151B s.4(10))
r-0018.requirement: A landlord may not discriminate against an applicant or tenant because they receive public assistance or a housing subsidy such as a Section 8 voucher, or because of the requirements of that program.
r-0018.key_value: No refusal based on public assistance or housing subsidy (vouchers)
r-0018.quoted_span: or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient
r-0018.title_es: Discriminación por fuente de ingresos y subsidio de vivienda (M.G.L. c.151B s.4(10))
r-0018.requirement_es: Un arrendador no puede discriminar a un solicitante o inquilino por recibir asistencia pública o un subsidio de vivienda, como un vale de Section 8, ni por los requisitos de ese programa.
r-0018.key_value_es: No se permite negarse por asistencia pública o subsidio de vivienda (vales)

r-0019.title: Criminal record (CORI) checks for housing applicants (803 CMR 5.00)
r-0019.requirement: A landlord, property manager or real estate agent may request a standard criminal record (CORI) check only on the housing applicant and only as the final step of the application, and may not use it to screen other household members.
r-0019.key_value: CORI only as the final step of the application; applicant only
r-0019.coverage_conditions: Landlords, property management companies and real estate agents evaluating applicants for market rate housing
r-0019.quoted_span: CORI shall only be requested for a housing applicant as the final step in the application process.
r-0019.interaction: Supplemental source: X029 (Cornell LII mirror of 803 CMR 5.04) because the supplied doc D056 was link-only (403). Effective date is the latest amendment shown (Mass Register Issue 1445, eff. 6/11/2021). Subsidized and public housing rules (5.05 and later) not read.

r-0021.requirement: Pending Senate bill to prohibit algorithmic rent setting; reported favorably by the Housing committee on 3/12/2026 and referred to Senate Ways and Means. It is not law.

r-0021.title_es: Aumento anual permitido de la Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) de Los Ángeles (Ordenanza de Estabilización de Alquileres)
r-0021.requirement_es: En unidades RSO el alquiler puede aumentarse una vez cada 12 meses según el porcentaje anual permitido que publica LAHD (3% del 2025-07-01 al 2026-06-30). Desde el cambio de fórmula no se permite ningún porcentaje adicional por servicios públicos ni por un dependiente añadido; el alquiler vuelve al precio de mercado solo después de una desocupación, como una mudanza voluntaria o una compra del contrato.
r-0021.key_value_es: % anual permitido por LAHD, una vez cada 12 meses (3% del 2025-07-01 al 2026-06-30); sin adicional por servicios públicos ni dependientes

r-0022.title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) annual allowable increase
r-0022.requirement: In RSO units rent may be raised once every 12 months by the annual allowable percentage published by LAHD (3% for 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30). Since the formula change no extra percentage for utilities or for an added dependent is allowed; rent resets to market only after a vacancy such as a voluntary move-out or buyout.
r-0022.key_value: LAHD annual allowable %, once per 12 months (3% for 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30); no utility or dependent add-on
r-0022.coverage_conditions: Rental properties first built on or before 1978-10-01 plus replacement units under L.A.M.C. 151.28: apartments, duplexes, two or more single-family dwellings on one parcel, ADUs, rooms rented over 30 days, mobile homes; condos and townhomes only for tenancies begun on or before 1995-12-31
r-0022.exemptions: Single-family dwelling alone on its parcel; condo or townhome tenancies begun after 1995-12-31 (rent not regulated); luxury exemption (by application, rent level on or before 1978-05-31); temporary exemptions on registration
r-0022.interaction: Takes precedence over the state cap Civ. Code 1947.12 for covered units. The rate page D042 shows 3% only through 2026-06-30; the 2026-27 percentage is not in the corpus. Non-RSO units fall under the state cap and the JCO.
r-0022.quoted_span: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage
r-0022.conflict_note: Two published effective dates for the new RSO formula: 2026-02-02 per LAHD (D041, D042, official, kept) and 2026-01-24 per a landlord association (reported in docs/starter_README.md section 9; that source is not in the corpus). Human review needed.

all.unavailable: single-family dwelling that is the only dwelling on its parcel
condominium or townhome tenancy commenced after 1995-12-31

r-0022.title_es: Just Cause Ordinance (JCO) de Los Ángeles, con causa justificada de la RSO para unidades RSO
r-0022.requirement_es: Un arrendador solo puede poner fin a un arrendamiento por una razón enumerada con culpa (falta de pago, violación del contrato, molestia, uso ilegal, negativa a renovar, negar el acceso, subarrendatario no aprobado) o sin culpa (mudanza del propietario o de un familiar, administrador residente, demolición o retiro del mercado, orden gubernamental, conversión), y debe pagar asistencia de reubicación en los desalojos sin culpa ($11,000 a $27,400 por unidad del 2026-07-01 al 2027-06-30).
r-0022.key_value_es: se requiere causa justificada; reubicación sin culpa de $11,000 a $27,400 (2026-07-01 a 2027-06-30)

r-0023.title: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO), with RSO just cause for RSO units
r-0023.requirement: A landlord may end a tenancy only for a listed at-fault reason (non-payment, lease violation, nuisance, illegal use, refusal to renew, denying access, unapproved subtenant) or no-fault reason (owner or family move-in, resident manager, demolition or removal from the market, government order, conversion), and must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions ($11,000 to $27,400 per unit for 2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30).
r-0023.key_value: just cause required; no-fault relocation $11,000 to $27,400 (2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30)
r-0023.coverage_conditions: JCO: most rental units not regulated by the RSO (buildings newer than 1978-10-01, a lone single-family dwelling), once the tenant has lived there six months or the original lease expired. RSO units (built on or before 1978-10-01) get the same just cause list under L.A.M.C. 151.09.
r-0023.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, some cooperatives, some nonprofit homeless or treatment facilities, some HACLA or government property
r-0023.interaction: Two LA instruments share this cell: the JCO (L.A.M.C. 165.00 et seq., non-RSO units, primary here) and the RSO eviction section L.A.M.C. 151.09 (RSO units, D041); both use the same causes and the same relocation chart (D043, Bulletin A), so one record covers every LA rental. Replaces state Civ. Code 1946.2 for covered property. JCO effective date not stated in the corpus.
r-0023.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
r-0023.title_es: Intereses sobre depósitos de seguridad según la RSO de Los Ángeles
r-0023.requirement_es: Los arrendadores de unidades RSO deben pagar a los inquilinos intereses sobre los depósitos de seguridad, mensual o anualmente, como pago directo o crédito en el alquiler, e informar por escrito al inquilino qué método usan. La Ciudad fija la tasa cada año (4.320% para el año calendario 2025).
r-0023.key_value_es: intereses sobre depósitos RSO, pagados mensual o anualmente (4.320% para 2025)

r-0024.title: Los Angeles RSO interest on security deposits
r-0024.requirement: Landlords of RSO units must pay tenants interest on security deposits, monthly or yearly, as a direct payment or rent credit, and tell the tenant in writing which method they use. The City sets the rate each year.
r-0024.key_value: annual interest on RSO security deposits (rate set yearly by LAHD)
r-0024.coverage_conditions: Units subject to the Los Angeles RSO (first built on or before 1978-10-01)
r-0024.interaction: Adds to, and does not replace, the state deposit cap Civ. Code 1950.5. D041 (LAHD) lists deposit interest among RSO requirements; the section number, payment rules and rates come from the AAGLA page X020 (secondary, supplemental source), which quotes interest accruing from 1990-11-01 (an accrual start, not the effective date of the current section, so effective_date stays null; latest rate shown there is 4.320% for 2025). No LA deposit cap found.
r-0024.title_es: Prohibición en Los Ángeles de la discriminación por fuente de ingresos (Section 8)
r-0024.requirement_es: Quien alquile una vivienda en Los Ángeles no puede negarse a alquilar ni a renovar, desalojar, fijar condiciones diferentes ni anunciar una preferencia basada en la fuente de ingresos de una persona, incluidos los vales de Section 8 y otras ayudas de alquiler. Los inquilinos pueden demandar por daños y usar una infracción como defensa ante un desalojo.
r-0024.key_value_es: no se permite negarse ni dar condiciones diferentes por fuente de ingresos (vales, ayuda de alquiler)

r-0025.title: Los Angeles ban on source-of-income (Section 8) discrimination
r-0025.requirement: Anyone renting housing in Los Angeles may not refuse to rent or renew, evict, set different terms, or advertise a preference based on a person's source of income, including Section 8 vouchers and other rental assistance. Tenants can sue for damages and use a violation as a defense to eviction.
r-0025.key_value: no refusal or different terms based on source of income (vouchers, rental assistance)
r-0025.coverage_conditions: All housing accommodations in the City of Los Angeles rented or offered for rent
r-0025.interaction: Supplemental source: no supplied D doc covers this ordinance (D038 is link-only), so X017 (codified text, sec. 45.69 effective 2020-01-01) is quoted and earns no citation credit. Adds to state FEHA (Gov. Code 12955). No LA criminal-history screening ordinance found in D040, D041, D043 or X017.
r-0025.quoted_span: Based upon a person’s source of income, refuse to rent or lease, or to continue to rent or lease, a housing accommodation;
r-0025.title_es: Rent Ordinance de San Francisco (Residential Rent Stabilization and Arbitration Ordinance)
r-0025.requirement_es: En unidades con control de alquileres, el arrendador puede aumentar el alquiler una vez al año según el aumento anual permitido por la Rent Board: 1.6% del 1 de marzo de 2026 al 28 de febrero de 2027 (1.4% el año anterior). Las unidades que obtuvieron por primera vez un certificado de ocupación después del 13 de junio de 1979 están exentas de estos límites de alquiler.

r-0026.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance (Residential Rent Stabilization and Arbitration Ordinance)
r-0026.requirement: In rent-controlled units, the landlord may raise the rent once a year by the Rent Board's annual allowable increase: 1.6% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 (1.4% the year before). Units that first got a certificate of occupancy after June 13, 1979 are exempt from these rent limits.
r-0026.coverage_conditions: Rental units with a certificate of occupancy on or before June 13, 1979
r-0026.exemptions: Units that first obtained a certificate of occupancy after June 13, 1979; tenancies eligible for a rent increase under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act; some tenancies whose rent is regulated by another government agency
r-0026.interaction: Local rent control; the California statewide cap (Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12) yields to it where it covers the unit. Rate confirmed by D083; the June 13, 1979 certificate-of-occupancy cutoff is stated in D079 and the brief.
r-0026.quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.
r-0026.title_es: Desalojo con causa justificada de la Rent Ordinance de San Francisco (Section 37.9)
r-0026.requirement_es: Un arrendador solo puede desalojar a un inquilino de una unidad cubierta por la Rent Ordinance por una de 17 causas justificadas enumeradas, y debe ser el motivo dominante; el vencimiento del contrato o un cambio de propietario no es una causa justificada. Los desalojos sin culpa, como la mudanza del propietario, activan pagos de reubicación.
r-0026.key_value_es: 17 causas justificadas; reubicación de $8,245 por inquilino, máximo $24,733 por unidad, más $5,497 por hogar con personas mayores, con discapacidad o con hijos menores (mudanza del propietario y similares, avisos entregados del 3/1/2026 al 2/28/2027)

r-0027.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance just cause eviction (Section 37.9)
r-0027.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance only for one of 17 listed just causes, and it must be the dominant motive; lease expiry or a change of owner is not a just cause. No-fault evictions such as owner move-in trigger relocation payments.
r-0027.key_value: 17 just causes; relocation $8,245 per tenant, max $24,733 per unit, plus $5,497 per elderly, disabled or minor-child household (owner move-in and similar, notices served 3/1/2026 to 2/28/2027)
r-0027.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the Rent Ordinance, including post-June 13, 1979 new construction and Costa-Hawkins tenancies that are exempt only from the rent limits
r-0027.exemptions: Some tenancies whose rent is regulated by another government agency (source gives no full list)
r-0027.interaction: Local just cause rule; the California statewide just cause rule (Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2) yields to it. Relocation amounts (Section 37.9C, Ellis Act amounts in 37.9A) from D082 and D083.
r-0027.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.
r-0027.title_es: Tasa de interés de depósitos de seguridad de San Francisco
r-0027.requirement_es: La Rent Board de San Francisco publica una tasa de interés anual que se aplica a los depósitos de seguridad de los inquilinos: 4.2% del 1 de marzo de 2026 al 28 de febrero de 2027 (5.0% el año anterior). La fuente indica la tasa, pero no la ordenanza ni su cobertura.
r-0027.key_value_es: 4.2% de interés sobre depósitos de seguridad (3/1/2026 a 2/28/2027)

r-0028.title: San Francisco security deposit interest rate
r-0028.requirement: The San Francisco Rent Board publishes an annual interest rate that applies to tenant security deposits: 4.2% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 (5.0% the year before). The source lists the rate but not the ordinance or its coverage.
r-0028.interaction: Adds an interest rate on deposits; the deposit cap itself is state law (Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5). Official code cite not in any supplied or gap-fill text.
r-0028.citation: S.F. Rent Board security deposit interest rate
r-0028.quoted_span: Security Deposit Interest: 4.2% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027
r-0028.title_es: Fair Chance Ordinance de San Francisco (vivienda)
r-0028.requirement_es: La Fair Chance Ordinance de San Francisco protege a las personas con antecedentes de arresto o condena en las decisiones de vivienda asequible. La fuente no da los detalles de lo que los arrendadores pueden preguntar ni cuándo.
r-0028.key_value_es: límites al uso de antecedentes de arresto o condena en decisiones de vivienda asequible

r-0029.title: San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, housing provisions (Police Code § 4906)
r-0029.requirement: For affordable housing, a housing provider may not ask about or use arrests without conviction, dismissed or expunged convictions, juvenile matters, convictions more than seven years old, infractions or decriminalized conduct, and may ask about conviction history only after finding the applicant eligible and qualified. Decisions need an individualized assessment, and the applicant gets 14 days to respond to a notice of adverse action.
r-0029.key_value: affordable housing only: no inquiry before eligibility check; 7-year look-back limit; individualized assessment; 14 days to respond to a notice of adverse action
r-0029.coverage_conditions: Housing providers, regarding applicants and household members for Affordable Housing (defined in § 4903, not in the corpus)
r-0029.interaction: Adds to state fair housing rules (Cal. Gov. Code § 12955). Quote from supplied D078, which names the ordinance only; X031 (city code library, supplemental source) supplies the official cite, the requirements and the dates (added by Ord. 17-14, operative 8/13/2014; last amended by Ord. 128-26, effective 8/10/2026).
r-0029.quoted_span: San Francisco's Fair Chance Ordinance protects residents with arrest or conviction history in affordable housing decisions.

applies_if.unavailable: affordable housing (the ordinance covers affordable housing decisions)

r-0029.title_es: Prohibición en San Francisco de dispositivos algorítmicos de fijación de alquileres
r-0029.requirement_es: Nadie puede vender ni usar un dispositivo algorítmico que analice datos no públicos de alquileres de competidores para recomendar alquileres o administrar la ocupación de unidades residenciales en San Francisco. Un inquilino o el City Attorney pueden demandar.
r-0029.key_value_es: prohibición de dispositivos algorítmicos que usan datos no públicos de alquileres de competidores

r-0030.title: San Francisco ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices
r-0030.requirement: No one may sell or use an algorithmic device that analyzes nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents or manage occupancy for residential units in San Francisco. A tenant or the City Attorney can sue.
r-0030.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor rental data
r-0030.interaction: Applies alongside the California statewide rules on common pricing algorithms (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (AB 325; SB 763)). X018 (law-firm alert) agrees on October 2024 and adds penalties up to $1,000 per violation per unit and month.
r-0030.quoted_span: adding Section 37.10C to the Rent Ordinance went into effect on October 14, 2024. The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.
r-0030.title_es: Residential Tenant Protections de San Diego (Tenant Protection Ordinance), causa justificada y reubicación
r-0030.requirement_es: Un arrendador no puede poner fin a un arrendamiento sin una causa justificada, con culpa o sin culpa. Para una terminación sin culpa, el arrendador debe pagar dos meses de alquiler (tres meses si el inquilino es una persona mayor o con discapacidad), o renunciar a esa cantidad de alquiler, sin importar los ingresos ni la duración del arrendamiento.
r-0030.key_value_es: se requiere causa justificada; reubicación sin culpa de 2 meses de alquiler (3 meses para personas mayores o con discapacidad)

r-0045.title: Hoboken Rent Control Ordinance
r-0045.requirement: At lease renewal a landlord of a rent-controlled Hoboken unit may not raise the rent by more than 5% or the CPI change, whichever is less, and only once in 12 months, with 30 days written notice explaining the reason. Tax, water/sewer and capital improvement surcharges need separate approval.
r-0045.key_value: Lesser of 5% or CPI change per year
r-0045.coverage_conditions: Dwellings to which Hoboken Code ch. 155 applies (coverage section 155-2 not in the captured text)
r-0045.exemptions: Newly constructed dwellings and buildings completely vacant since January 1, 1984, on determination by the Rent Regulation Officer; vacancy decontrol (art. VII) and condo/co-op initial rental decontrol (art. VIII); criteria not in the captured text
r-0045.quoted_span: no landlord may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than 5% or the percentage difference between the consumer price index
r-0045.interaction: Supplemental source: Hoboken ecode pages (X001 to X003) have no supplied D-doc equivalent. effective_date is the adoption date of Ord. B-532 (2-1-2023), the history tag over section 155-5 (cap); chapter adopted 1-16-1984 (X001). Coverage and exemption criteria are not captured, so the exemption stays unknown for every address.
r-0045.title_es: Prohibición en Hoboken de la fijación de precios mediante precios algorítmicos
r-0045.requirement_es: Los arrendadores de cualquier unidad de vivienda residencial en Hoboken no pueden usar software, algoritmos ni plataformas de intercambio de datos que analicen información no pública de competidores para coordinar, recomendar o implementar alquileres, condiciones del contrato o niveles de ocupación. Las infracciones se juzgan en la Hoboken Municipal Court.
r-0045.key_value_es: Prohibición de precios algorítmicos con datos no públicos de competidores (de menos de 365 días); multa de hasta $2,000 o hasta 90 días de servicio comunitario

r-0046.title: Hoboken ban on price fixing using algorithmic pricing
r-0046.requirement: Landlords of any residential dwelling unit in Hoboken may not use software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms that analyze nonpublic competitor information to coordinate, recommend or implement rents, lease terms or occupancy levels. Violations go to Hoboken Municipal Court.
r-0046.key_value: Ban on algorithmic pricing using nonpublic competitor data (under 365 days old); fine up to $2,000 or up to 90 days community service
r-0046.coverage_conditions: Any residential dwelling unit used as a primary residence in Hoboken
r-0046.quoted_span: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing.
r-0046.interaction: Supplemental source (codified text X003, adopted 7-9-2025 by Ord. B-781; X018 and the brief say effective July 2025, consistent). Possible preemption by the NJ FAIR Act from 2027-07-01 (human review via conflicts_with).
r-0046.title_es: Rent Control Ordinance de Newark (Ordenanza de Control de Alquileres)
r-0046.requirement_es: En la renovación del contrato, un arrendador de Newark no puede aumentar el alquiler más que el cambio del CPI-U entre 15 y 3 meses antes, y nunca más del 4%, una vez cada 12 meses, con aviso escrito de 30 días. No se permite ningún aumento si la vivienda no cumple sustancialmente con el código o no está registrada.
r-0046.key_value_es: Cambio del CPI-U, máximo 4% por 12 meses

all.unavailable: Rent Control Board certification of newly constructed multiple dwelling exemption (19:2-18.1)

r-0047.title: Newark Rent Control Ordinance
r-0047.requirement: At lease renewal a Newark landlord may not raise rent by more than the CPI-U change over the prior 15 to 3 months, and never more than 4%, once per 12 months, with 30 days written notice. No increase is allowed if the dwelling is not in substantial code compliance or not registered.
r-0047.coverage_conditions: All multiple dwellings in Newark (any building with one or more apartments rented or offered for rent)
r-0047.exemptions: Public housing; transient hotel/motel space; commercial space; newly constructed multiple dwellings certified by the Rent Control Board, for 30 years after completion or the initial mortgage amortization period if shorter (19:2-18.1); substantially rehabilitated vacant dwellings for 5 years (19:2-18.2); Rental Rehabilitation Program units with Section 8; units under a government rent-regulation contract
r-0047.quoted_span: In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed 4%.

r-0047.title_es: Ordenanza de vivienda Ban the Box de Newark (Newark Ban the Box)
r-0047.requirement_es: Los arrendadores y corredores solo pueden verificar antecedentes penales después de una solicitud formal, con aviso y consentimiento, y solo pueden revisar 8 años atrás para condenas por delitos mayores (indictable) o 5 años para infracciones de personas desordenadas (disorderly persons) (más delitos graves enumerados y cargos pendientes). No pueden usarse arrestos sin condena, registros eliminados (expunged) ni de menores, y las denegaciones requieren razones por escrito.

r-0048.title: Newark Ban the Box housing ordinance
r-0048.requirement: Landlords and brokers may check criminal history only after a formal application, with notice and consent, and may look back only 8 years for indictable convictions or 5 years for disorderly persons offenses (plus listed serious offenses and pending charges). Arrests without conviction, expunged and juvenile records may not be used, and denials need written reasons.
r-0048.key_value: Criminal history inquiry only after a formal application; 8-year / 5-year lookback; fines up to $500 first, $1,000 repeat
r-0048.coverage_conditions: Rental, lease or sublease of real property by a landlord or real estate broker in Newark
r-0048.exemptions: Single apartment in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling; rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling; where federal or state law requires or permits criminal history consideration; property in a government program housing people with criminal histories
r-0048.quoted_span: Inquiry into and consideration of any applicant's criminal history shall take place only after the applicant has submitted a formal application.

r-0049.quoted_span: The Housing Stability Notification Act requires any landlord to provide renters with a Notice of Tenant’s Rights and Resources when planning to end a tenancy agreement.

no_rule.note: San Diego's tenant protection division has no rent cap, and the notice it requires landlords to give (S.D.M.C. 98.0705) sends tenants to state Civ. Code 1947.12 for rent limits, while it says 'Local law also provides' only for just cause. X027 (LASSD FAQ) repeats this notice. So state 1947.12 governs San Diego rents.

D039 is a 2024-09-03 council motion that only asks LAHD to report on feasibility of a ban. The Morgan Lewis survey of local algorithmic rent laws dated 2026-08-21 (X018) lists San Francisco, San Diego, Berkeley and Santa Ana but not Los Angeles, and the brief's examples omit LA. State Bus. & Prof. Code 16729 still applies.

The brief's illustrative San Francisco lookup cites only Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6 for the screening fee while layering local rules in the rent, just cause and algorithmic rows; no supplied SF doc (D078 to D083) names a local fee rule. Medium confidence: no SF text positively says there is none.

Massachusetts has no statewide just-cause eviction statute: c.186 s.12 (D051) lets either party end a tenancy at will by written notice without cause; c.186 s.11 and s.31 (D050, D058) are notice-to-quit rules for nonpayment and s.18 (D053) is anti-retaliation, none limits the grounds for eviction.
